name: The path of the two stages (Indian Vajrayāna)

stages.name: abhiṣeka
stages.description: Entry into the maṇḍala and the four consecrations from a vajra master.

stages.name: samaya
stages.description: Keeping the pledges and avoiding the root downfalls; the three vows.

stages.name: utpattikrama
stages.description: Deity yoga: arising as the deity in the maṇḍala, mantra, service.

stages.name: utpattikrama (stable)
stages.description: Clarity and pride of the deity stabilized; the 'staircase' to the completion stage.

stages.name: utpannakrama
stages.description: Winds drawn into the central channel; isolations, empties, illusory body; or the six-branch yoga.

stages.name: prabhāsvara
stages.description: Direct realization of clear light (the all-empty).

stages.name: yuganaddha (śaikṣa)
stages.description: Union of illusory body and clear light still to be cultivated.

stages.name: yuganaddha (aśaikṣa) / Vajradhara
stages.description: Buddhahood in this very life: non-dual gnosis, non-abiding nirvāṇa.

stages.name: samayamudrā
stages.description: Vajradhara radiating as Heruka with enjoyment and emanation bodies for beings.

notes: A composite map assembled by the unit from the cited texts; the 'learner/non-learner' split of union is the later scholastic presentation.

name: The five stages of the Pañcakrama (Ārya Guhyasamāja)

stages.name: utpattikrama
stages.description: The practitioner established in the generation stage.

stages.name: vajrajāpa (vāgviveka)
stages.description: Mantra joined with the winds.

stages.name: sarvaśuddhiviśuddhi (cittaviveka)
stages.description: The three appearances and four empties with the eighty natural conceptions.

stages.name: svādhiṣṭhāna
stages.description: The illusory body, conventional truth, by the guru's grace.

stages.name: abhisambodhi
stages.description: Clear light, the all-empty, ultimate truth.

stages.name: yuganaddha
stages.description: Union of illusory body and clear light; buddhahood as Vajradhara.

name: The six-limbed service of the Guhyasamāja (ch. 18)

stages.name: pratyāhāra
stages.description: The ten senses resting in their own places; blessed by all mantras.

stages.name: dhyāna
stages.description: The five objects of desire as the five buddhas, fivefold; the five superknowledges.

stages.name: prāṇāyāma
stages.description: The five-gnosis breath as a jewel at the nose tip; blessed by bodhisattvas.

stages.name: dhāraṇā
stages.description: Mantra in the heart in the drop of life-wind; the five signs; Vajrasattva enters.

stages.name: anusmṛti
stages.description: Recollecting the visualized form, an appearance arises; a halo of light.

stages.name: samādhi
stages.description: Sudden arising of gnosis; free of obscurations.

notes: Verse numbers are the unit's count in Bhattacharya's e-text; bands are interpretive. U51 owns the Kālacakra version (pth:kalacakra-six-branches), which has the same order of limbs.

stages.name: rtogs pa skyed
stages.description: First the intelligent generate realization (from the true guru).

stages.name: gnas lugs ma yengs sgom
stages.gloss: undistracted meditation on the natural state
stages.description: Meditating without distraction; making all appearances undivided.

stages.name: spyod pa
stages.description: When experience has arisen, practising conduct with care — for Mekopa the cremation ground and the 'mad' observance.

name: Torrent, river, ocean (Tilopa's Gaṅgā Mahāmudrā)

stages.name: gcong rong chu
stages.description: Beginning practice, turbulent.

stages.name: chu bo gang+gA
stages.description: Middle practice, steady.

stages.name: chu bran ma bu phrad
stages.gloss: river meeting the ocean, mother and child
stages.description: Final realization.

notes: Correspondence with the later four yogas of mahāmudrā (pth:mahamudra-four-yogas) is not stated by Tilopa.
